content: The medication is administered subcutaneously, typically in the upper arms, buttocks, thighs, or abdomen. It is important not to shake the medication. The product may contain a few small white particles, which is normal. However, before use, inspect the medication for any other particles or discoloration. If such abnormalities are present, do not use the medication. Prior to each injection, clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol. Rotate the injection site with each dose to minimize the risk of skin injury. Avoid injecting into skin that is irritated, sore, or infected. To reduce bruising, refrain from rubbing the injection site after administration. This medication should be used consistently to achieve the maximum therapeutic benefit. Common side effects may include bruising, itching, pain, redness, swelling, or hardening of the skin at the injection site. These reactions typically resolve within one to two days. Other possible side effects include headache, back pain, or sinus and throat pain. This medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks. It can affect your immune system by reducing your body’s ability to fight infections. As a result, you may be more susceptible to serious infections, such as those affecting the lungs, bones, joints, skin, sinuses, or gastrointestinal system. It may also impair your ability to combat existing infections. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience persistent nausea or vomiting, worsening redness, swelling, or tenderness at the injection site after two days, fever, chills, flu-like symptoms, painful or frequent urination, unusual vaginal discharge, burning, itching, or odor, or severe abdominal pain. This medication may rarely cause a condition known as posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES), which can be life-threatening. Additionally, there is a rare risk of developing cancer, including skin cancer, associated with this medication. Discuss the risks and benefits of treatment with your doctor. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are rare but possible. This is not an exhaustive list of potential side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar concerns. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients, such as natural rubber or latex in the needle cover of the prefilled syringe, which could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may increase your susceptibility to infections or worsen existing infections. Do not receive immunizations or vaccinations without your doctor’s approval, and avoid contact with individuals who have recently received live vaccines, such as oral polio or nasal flu vaccines. Avoid receiving BCG vaccines for one year after completing treatment with this medication. Additionally, stay away from individuals with contagious infections, such as chickenpox, COVID-19, measles, or the flu. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. It may pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of this medication or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. In the event of an overdose with serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911 in the U.S.) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While using this medication, regular laboratory and medical tests, such as skin exams, should be conducted. Ensure you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist promptly to establish a new dosing schedule. Different brands of this medication may have different storage requirements. Refer to the product packaging for specific storage instructions or consult your pharmacist. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
